title: Tiktaalik roseae
summary: Tiktaalik roseae is a fish about 375 million years old, found in 2004 on Ellesmere Island, Nunavut. Its front fins contain an arm-like internal skeleton with joints but lack clear fingers, and researchers described it in Nature in 2006 as a missing link between fish and land animals.

uncertainty.note: Both opened pages say about 375 million years; no error range stated.

where.historical_name: River delta on the Devonian equator, Laurussia (no human geography)

paleo.plate_model: MERDITH2021 (Merdith et al. 2021, Earth-Science Reviews 214:103477) via GPlates Web Service
paleo.note: Island centroid 79.62, -76.77 reconstructed to 375 Ma; the find site is a specific locality on the island.

importance.justification: A transitional fossil showing fish features and limb-like fin bones, used to illustrate the move onto land.
